speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these bleeding episodes and petechiae? Have you noticed any other symptoms like joint pain, abdominal pain, or unusual bruising?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Has the child had any recent viral illnesses, and is there any family history of bleeding disorders or easy bruising? I also need to know if the child has had any recent medications or if there are any signs of bleeding elsewhere, such as in the urine or stool.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: To help narrow down the cause, has the child had any recent fevers, bone pain, or night sweats, and do you notice any enlarged lymph nodes or an enlarged liver/spleen on exam? I will also request a complete blood count with differential and a peripheral blood smear to check for platelet levels and cell morphology. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Differential

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count effectively rules out thrombocytopenia, suggesting a qualitative platelet defect or a coagulation factor issue. To distinguish between these, does the bleeding stop with pressure, and have you noticed any deep tissue bruising or joint bleeding (hemarthrosis)? REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal bleeding time and platelet count make a primary platelet disorder unlikely, pointing toward a coagulation factor deficiency. To differentiate between hemophilia and von Willebrand disease, I need to assess for joint bleeding and mucosal patterns. Does the child have a family history of bleeding disorders, particularly on the maternal side, and have you observed any swelling or pain in the knees or elbows? REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time_and_Partial_Thromboplastin_Time

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal platelet count, bleeding time, PT, and aPTT, the most likely diagnosis is von Willebrand disease, which can present with normal standard coagulation screens. I will request specific testing for von Willebrand factor antigen and activity to confirm. REQUEST TEST: von_Willebrand_Factor_Antigen_and_Activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: This finding of deficient GIIb/IIIa receptors on platelet surfaces is diagnostic for Glanzmann thrombasthenia, a qualitative platelet disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
